correctness.rationale: A symmetric circulant is an inversion-fixed polynomial in R=F_q[X]/(X^n-1), normalized by f(1)=1. In odd field characteristic ℓ, reduction to S=F_q[X]/(X^m-1), n=ℓ^s m, is surjective on involution invariants by averaging and has q^((n-m)/2) uniform normalized lifts. Reconstructed the decomposition of nonfixed roots under Frobenius and negation into factors F_(q^e), with fixed root 1 and an extra -1 factor iff m even. The determinant is (product of norms)^(2ℓ^s) for m odd, and v^(ℓ^s)(product of norms)^(2ℓ^s) for m even; nilpotents do not affect the determinant. Surjective finite-field norms give the exact even uniform fibers, odd square-only fibers, and pure-ℓ-power determinant-one exception, including n1. Independently enumerated symmetric first rows and evaluated determinants by finite-field Gaussian elimination at q3 n2..6 and q5 n3,4; all individual fibers matched formulas. Finite checks were corroboration of the general finite-field algebra proof.

value.rationale: Complete determinant-fiber distribution for every symmetric circulant row-sum-normalized matrix over odd finite fields is a natural algebraic invariant. The even/odd/special-characteristic trichotomy explains exact arithmetic obstructions and supplies zero, square and every nonzero determinant counts, going beyond mere invertibility tests.

limitations: Any odd prime-power field q; n≥1; symmetric circulants with row sum exactly one. No characteristic-two, sparsity or orthogonal-circulant claim.
